Part A: Key Institutional & Student-Centric Committees

Part A: Key Institutional & Student-Centric Committees
S. No.CommitteeMottoResponsibilities
1Student Welfare CommitteeFostering Student Growth, Equity, and Holistic Well-BeingDedicated to overseeing the overall physical, academic, and socio-emotional welfare of students on campus. It provides comprehensive pastoral support, identifies student needs, and ensures access to essential campus resources, recreational avenues, and health services. The committee actively bridges communication between learners and administration to maintain an enriching, balanced collegiate journey.
2College Disciplinary Committee (CDC)Upholding Integrity, Professional Decorum, and Campus HarmonyResponsible for enforcing institutional discipline, ethics, and code of conduct across college blocks, hospital wards, and residential hostels. It conducts fair and transparent inquiries into reported misconduct, attendance irregularities, examination malpractice, and property damage. The committee emphasizes corrective interventions and character building while maintaining institutional dignity.
3Student Mental Health & Wellness Committee (SMHWC)Nurturing Minds, Enhancing Resilience, and destigmatizing CareA proactive body established to promote psychological well-being, mitigate academic stress, and provide timely emotional guidance to undergraduate students. Working closely with faculty mentors, institutional psychiatrists, and clinical psychologists, it conducts regular wellness workshops and screening sessions. It also facilitates confidential access to national support systems like the 24x7 TELE-MANAS helpline.
4Student Grievance Redressal Committee (SGRC)Ensuring Fairness, Transparency, and Timely Conflict ResolutionProvides a structured, impartial, and confidential mechanism for students to lodge complaints regarding academic, administrative, or infrastructural matters. It guarantees unbiased hearings and objective fact-finding to redress grievances efficiently without fear of reprisal. The committee ensures strict compliance with regulatory standards to safeguard student rights.
5Anti-Ragging Committee (ARC) & Anti-Ragging Flying Squad (ARS)Zero Tolerance to Ragging; Fostering Mutual Respect and DignityMandated by statutory NMC and state regulations to prevent, prohibit, and eliminate ragging in all forms within and beyond the campus. The apex committee formulates preventive safeguards and investigates complaints, while the Flying Squad conducts round-the-clock physical vigil and surprise raids across hostels, dining messes, and transit zones. Any infraction is met with swift, stringent disciplinary and legal action.
6College Council CommitteeCollaborative Leadership and Integrated Institutional GovernanceServes as the apex administrative council comprising the Principal as Chairperson and all Heads of Departments as members. Meeting at least quarterly, it reviews institutional operations, student welfare, academic progress, clinical administration, and hospital services. The council ensures cohesive coordination across departments to uphold regulatory standards and educational excellence.
7Curriculum CommitteeOutcome-Driven Excellence through Competency-Based LearningOversees the effective design, implementation, and quality assurance of the NMC Competency-Based Medical Education (CBME) curriculum. It plans horizontal and vertical integration, monitors timetables, reviews internal assessment blueprints, and coordinates foundation courses, electives, and AETCOM modules. The committee regularly updates academic delivery based on feedback from departmental heads and student representatives.
8Committee for Prevention of Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace / Internal Complaints CommitteeSafety, Dignity, and Zero Tolerance for Workplace HarassmentConstituted under the statutory provisions of the POSH Act, 2013, to ensure a secure, respectful, and gender-inclusive working and learning environment for female students, faculty, and healthcare staff. It spearheads awareness campaigns on gender equity and rights across campus. The committee conducts prompt, confidential, and empathetic inquiry into complaints, recommending stringent corrective and punitive measures.
9Gender Harassment CommitteePromoting Gender Equity, Sensitization, and InclusivityWorks in synergy with institutional equity cells to promote mutual respect, non-discrimination, and gender sensitization across the campus community. It regularly conducts interactive seminars, orientation sessions, and open forums to build an environment free from gender bias. The committee handles grievances concerning gender-based discrimination with utmost discretion and sensitivity.
10Hostel Advisory Committee (HAC)Creating a Safe, Comfortable, and Disciplined Home Away from HomeDedicated to overseeing the management, security, sanitation, and living standards across the undergraduate and postgraduate residential blocks. Comprising wardens, faculty representatives, and student nominees, it coordinates hostel maintenance, enforces curfew and visitor protocols, and monitors mess nutrition and hygiene. The committee ensures the hostels remain safe, comfortable, and conducive to academic focus.
11Anti-Drug Committee (ADC)Vigilant, Resilient, and 100% Drug-Free CampusConstituted in alignment with directives from the Telangana Anti-Narcotics Bureau (TG-NAB), KNRUHS, and district administration to eradicate substance abuse. It drives continuous awareness on the hazards of narcotics and alcohol through peer policing, guest lectures, and student pledge drives. In coordination with local law enforcement, it carries out surprise inspections and strictly penalizes violations under the NDPS Act.

Part B: Other Statutory, Academic & Clinical Committees

Part B: Other Statutory, Academic & Clinical Committees
S. No.CommitteeResponsibilities
12Medical Education Unit (MEU)Drives faculty development programs, basic/advanced medical education technology workshops, and modern instructional design.
13Institutional Ethics Committee (IEC - Human Studies)Operates under DHR (Department of Health Research) and CDSCO (Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation) approvals to ensure ethical review of all biomedical research.
14Institutional Animal Ethics Committee (IAEC)Regulates laboratory research and animal-assisted learning in compliance with CPCSEA guidelines.
15Scientific & Research Advisory CommitteePromotes, evaluates, and monitors faculty, postgraduate, and student research dissertations, publications, and ICMR projects.
16Hospital Infection Control Committee (HICC)Monitors healthcare-associated infections (HAI), enforces sterilization standards, and leads antibiotic stewardship programs.
17Pharmacovigilance CommitteeActively monitors, records, and reports adverse drug reactions (ADRs) to the national Pharmacovigilance Programme of India (PvPI).
18Hospital Security & Safety CommitteeOversees 24x7 integrated CCTV surveillance, campus access control, emergency disaster preparedness, and fire safety protocols.
19Mortality & Death Audit CommitteeConducts regular clinical audits and death review meetings to ensure high clinical care standards and diagnostic accuracy.

Medical, dental and nursing education.
